Alex K.: Heads-up: migration of prod-gpu-cluster to us-west-2 starts tomorrow morning. We need temporary increases for EBS throughput and snapshot API limits — hitting bottlenecks during the dry run. Can someone open an AWS limit case?
Maria G.: OK — what exact limits did we hit in the run? numbers help the support case.
Alex K.: Observed: nightly checkpoints created ~400 concurrent snapshots, avg completion ~8-10h, CreateSnapshot throttling errors at scale. Also per-volume throughput caps when attaching 100+ worker volumes simultaneously. Region: us-west-2, account: 123456789012.
Will C.: Confirming attach volume errors: lots of AttachVolume throttles and a few ENI allocation warnings during parallel node bring-up. This is blocking fast scale-up for the migration tests.
InfraBot: [alert] 1793204120 - snapshot-backlog-us-west-2 - pending_snapshots=372 avg_completion_seconds=30000 :warning:
Maria G.: Ok, proposal for the form to submit to AWS Support (pasteable):
```
Service: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS)
Region: us-west-2
Account ID: 123456789012
Requested increases:
  - Concurrent CreateSnapshot throughput (CreateSnapshot API): from 20/sec -> 120/sec
  - Max pending snapshots per account: from 500 -> 2500
  - Per-volume throughput (MB/s) for gp3/io2 volumes: from 1000 -> 4000
  - Regional total number of Provisioned IOPS volumes (io2/io1) and aggregate IOPS quota: increase to support 120,000 IOPS burst
  - EC2 AttachVolume API throttling: increase attach rate to support 500 attachments/min during scaling
Justification: Migrating prod-gpu-cluster (120 GPU workers) with nightly 1TB incremental checkpoints. Without these increases we see CreateSnapshot throttling and attach failures, causing multi-hour scale-up regressions and potential downtime. We request temporary quota increases for the migration window plus a permanent uplift for steady-state throughput.
```
Will C.: Nice. Add that snapshots are largely incremental but we do many parallel tasks that hit the snapshot-create path at the same time. Also mention we can provide CloudWatch graphs if they ask.
Alex K.: On it. Filing now. I'll add cost/backing docs and a timeline.
Alex K.: Case created: AWS-CASE-2027-98765 (Business Support). Support asked for architecture diagram and a rough schedule for the migration. Pasted the short architecture note below.
```
Architecture summary:
  - 120 GPU worker fleet across 10 ASGs in us-west-2 (p3/p4 instances)
  - Each worker mounts a 1TB gp3 volume for checkpoints (snapshots at end-of-shift, ~6 hours window)
  - Controller creates snapshots concurrently during a rolling checkpoint window to minimize impact.
  - Peak parallel snapshot ops observed when rolling windows align across clusters and CI jobs.
```
Ops SRE: Re: ENI warnings — also check EC2 IP address quotas in the AZs. When we spin up 120 nodes quickly we sometimes hit Elastic IP/ENI limits per account per AZ. Might be worth adding a short note to the case asking them to validate ENI allocation caps.
Maria G.: Good call. Also attaching a short mitigation plan to reduce blast radius if support escalation takes time: staggered snapshot windows, add 30s jitter on snapshot-create, and temp increase of retention to avoid concurrent deletes. Example cron: `0 2-6/1 * * *` with jitter script.
Will C.: I added CloudWatch links and graphs to the AWS case. Support replied asking for a contact for technical callbacks — suggested we provide an SRE pager alias.
Alex K.: Provided pager alias: ops-pager@redwood.ai and requested expedited review. Marking priority: migration-critical.
InfraBot: [update] 1793205300 - aws-case-update - AWS acknowledged and asked for escalation window details.
Alex K.: Thanks. Will monitor the case and post updates. If we get a partial increase we can still optimize our schedule. :thumbsup:
Maria G.: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround.
Ops SRE: Once we have quota uplift, let's run another smoke test with a 40-node burst and watch AttachVolume/ENI metrics.
Alex K.: Plan accepted. I'll coordinate the smoke test after case approval.
